item.title: Optimization of Urban Shortest Path Considering Traffic Congestion and Air Quality Using ICAW and Genetic Algorithm (Case Study: Tehran)
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — This study proposes a multi-objective framework for optimizing urban shortest paths by simultaneously considering traffic congestion and air quality. The objective is to minimize a weighted combination of travel time and pollutant exposure, with binary decision variables representing route selection. Real-world air quality data (SO₂, NO₂, CO) were collected from IoT sensors on 500 vehicles and 50 fixed stations across Tehran, integrated with traffic data via spatio-temporal synchronization using inverse distance weighting and 500m grid mapping. item.title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. item.description: Computers, materials & continua/Computers, materials & continua (Print) — Fire threatens human life, property, and ecosystems, and recent years have seen frequent fire incidents worldwide. Video surveillance combined with deep learning has become a common strategy for fire and smoke detection. However, existing detectors often lose accuracy and robustness when targets are small, amorphous, or blurred against complex outdoor backgrounds. item.title: Bridging the Educational Gap with Virtual Reality (VR): Virtual Labs for the Next Generation
item.description: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science — This research addresses the systemic educational inequality in Thailand, where a severe shortage of physical science laboratories in rural areas hinders the development of 21st-century scientific literacy. Using the ADDIE model, the study developed a virtual world technology innovation, the AR SciLab platform, to serve as a high-quality, risk-free learning infrastructure. The innovation comprises a database of eight career-oriented experiments (e.g., biodiesel production and essential oil extraction), 3D immersive VR environments built on Unreal Engine 5, and bilingual instructional media. item.description: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation) — Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. This study develops a physical--digital activity-space framework that distinguishes co-presence, digital exposure, and digital interaction, and represents physical and digital segregation as separate components rather than a forced composite. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — This research evaluates the socioeconomic feasibility of expanding the aerial cable car system in Manizales and Villamaría, Colombia, through a Social Cost-Benefit Analysis (SCBA). The assessment compares the three operational lines with a projected nine-line network, based on the Manizales Land Use Plan. The objective is to quantify and monetize impacts on CO2eq emissions, territorial accessibility, road safety, and public health benefits derived from induced active mobility. item.description: Geosport for Society — This study conceptualizes the EuroLeague as a transnational urban network and tests whether spatial position and nominal travel distance are associated with competitive outcomes. The design integrates three empirical layers: (i) a longitudinal spatial panel covering the league-format era from 2016-17 to 2025-26; (ii) a completed 2025- 26 cross-section of 20 clubs in 17 nominal urban nodes and 11 countries; and (iii) a game-level model based on 1,943 available regular-season games from seven analytically retained seasons between 2016-17 and 2024-25. item.title: STRATEGIC SPATIAL PLANNING FOR ENHANCING THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF THE TOURISM SECTOR IN GOA, INDIA
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. item.title: MORE MONUMENTS, MORE TOURISTS? EXAMINING HERITAGE-TOURISM RELATIONSHIPS ACROSS ROMANIAN COUNTIES
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Cultural heritage is an important territorial resource for tourism development, yet the relationship between the distribution of listed heritage assets and tourism activity remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the geographical relationships between listed cultural heritage and tourism in Romania, focusing on territorial disparities and long-term changes. item.title: Rethinking Women’s Football Attendance in an Emerging Destination: Constraints, Marketing Awareness and Interest through a Pluriversal Lens
item.description: Geosport for Society — Women’s football is increasingly recognised as an important component of the sport tourism industry, with potential to diversify audiences, stimulate domestic travel, and advance gender inclusivity in emerging destinations. Yet, despite the growing interest, attendance remains inconsistent, complicating conventional measures of spectator demand. item.description: Revista de Aplicaciones de la Ingeniería — In this article we highlight the importance of monitoring polluting particles in cities. This is to contribute to achieving sustainability objectives. Air pollution by suspended particles, especially PM2.5 and PM10, is a serious public health problem in urban areas of Mexico, with measurable impacts on respiratory and cardiovascular mortality and morbidity. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Illegal trade in lobster pueruli (Benih Bening Lobster, BBL) presents interconnected challenges for fisheries governance, coastal livelihoods, and Indonesia’s maritime defense. This study examines how changes in BBL utilization policies, legal market access, and commodity traceability create potential vulnerabilities that may be exploited by smuggling networks. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Indonesia’s customs administration operates at the intersection of maritime mobility, trade facilitation, border protection, and revenue assurance, yet its risk systems are still primarily organized around declarations, manifests, entities, and transactions rather than the wider maritime operating picture. This article develops a conceptual model for transforming Maritime Domain Awareness into a Customs Risk Picture that can support earlier, more contextual, and more explainable targeting of vessels, voyages, cargoes, and commercial actors. item.title: Between emergency and reconstruction: Territorial impacts and climate adaptation challenges after hurricane John in Guerrero
item.description: ECORFAN eBooks — This chapter analyses the territorial, human, and socioeconomic impacts caused by Hurricane John (2024) in the state of Guerrero, with a particular focus on the municipalities of Acapulco and Coyuca de Benítez, within a context of increasing intensity and frequency of extreme hydrometeorological events. item.description: Jurnal Al-Ijtimaiyyah — The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru not only destroyed homes but also severed the social and economic networks of thousands of families in Lumajang Regency, demanding a disaster response grounded in Islamic normative principles alongside technical capacity. Muhammadiyah, through the Himpunan Putusan Tarjih (HPT), has formulated Disaster Fiqh as an ethical framework to safeguard the rights of disaster victims, yet studies examining how far humanitarian organizations’ field practices align with this framework at the family level remain scarce. item.description: Journal Labor and Demographic economics — This article examines the relationship between ancestral knowledge, artisanal production, and socioeconomic benefits in Tabasco through an integrative review of academic literature and official documents. The corpus covers embroidered strips, plant fibers, wood carving, drum making, and workshop organization, together with cultural statistics, legislation, and public programs. By means of social mobility, people with disability receive access to various public benefits and possibility to lead comprehensively rich life. item.description: AIS Electronic Library (AISeL) — Digital content platforms must recommend new content before knowing its quality or audience fit, while early feedback is selectively shaped by prior allocation rules. Although exploration may support learning, direct evidence is limited regarding whether early random exploration improves the subsequent organic recommendation performance of new content by generating more informative feedback. item.title: Contribution of agricultural cooperatives and humanitarian assistance on food security resilience and rural development in Mali
item.description: ORBi (University of Liège) — Mali, located in the Sahel region, experiences a persistent food security crisis driven by climate variability, recurrent conflict, displacement, market disruptions, and structural weaknesses in rural systems. The agricultural sector, which supports the majority of households, is highly vulnerable to droughts, erratic rainfall, flooding, and insecurity. item.title: Comparative Framework of Vulnerability in Coastal Communities of the Ecuadorian Tropics
item.description: Applied Planetary Health — This study conducts a comparative analysis of socio-ecological vulnerability in six coastal communities of the Ecuadorian tropics, integrating mixed methods (quantitative and qualitative). The conceptual framework based on the components of Exposure, Sensitivity, and Adaptive Capacity allowed the construction of a Comparative Coastal Vulnerability Index (CCVI). item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distribution and environmental degradation can reinforce one another. Emerging prominently during the 1970s and 1980s, eco-feminism has developed from an early emphasis on the symbolic relationship between women and nature toward broader approaches involving environmental justice, political ecology, intersectionality and sustainable development. item.description: Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University) — This research explored how access to everyday destinations influences neighborhood and social satisfaction among individuals with disabilities. It examined how factors such as sociodemographic characteristics, accessibility, and frequency of visits to places contribute to how people experience their neighborhoods and social lives. item.description: PubMed Central — Background: Climate change is increasing the extent of wildfires and extreme heat events (EHEs) in the Western United States. Our objective was to estimate the risk of all-cause mortality and hospitalization among end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients after exposure to wildfire smoke, EHEs, and the combined occurrence of wildfire smoke and EHE. item.title: Urban Context and Travel Experience Events: An Exploratory Comparison of Two German Cities
item.description: AHFE international — The presented study investigates associations between events influencing public transportation experience in both urban (Hamburg) and rural (Tuttlingen) areas in Germany, with the aim of identifying events associated with travel experience, which may in turn influence travel behavior. Using a mobile application, 21 participants in Tuttlingen and 70 participants in Hamburg tracked everyday trips, providing real-time evaluations of travel experiences along with situational data. item.description: Journal of Ecological Engineering — Lateritic nickel mining can increase the transport of metal-bearing particles into river systems, where sediment–water partitioning governs metal mobility and ecological exposure. Although redox conditions and organic matter are recognized as factors associated with metal partitioning, their relative importance under tropical lateritic mining conditions remains poorly understood. item.description: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University) — Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH), including neighborhood conditions, structural racism, and socioeconomic disadvantage, contribute to disease development and progression. item.title: Decolonizing ecocriticism: Climate justice, Indigenous knowledge, and more-than-human agency in contemporary Anglophone literature
item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Contemporary climate fiction increasingly challenges the assumption that ecological crisis can be understood exclusively through universalized narratives of environmental degradation. Such narratives often obscure the historical inequalities through which ecological harm is produced and unevenly distributed. This article proposes a decolonizing approach to ecocriticism through a comparative reading of Imbolo Mbue’s How Beautiful We Were (2021) and Amitav Ghosh’s Gun Island (2019). item.description: CAUCHY Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi — Infrastructure development is important for reducing regional disparities, but Indonesian provinces differ in economic conditions, human resources, and regional characteristics. This study examines the relationships between the Economy, Human Resources, and Regional Characteristics and Infrastructure in the 38 provinces of Indonesia, based on secondary data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS) for 2024 and 2025. item.title: Urban retail contraction reveals a spatial vulnerability trap in essential retail access
item.description: Research Square — Grocery stores, pharmacies, and other essential retailers anchor daily life, but in U.S. cities they are closing unevenly. These closures do more than remove nearby options. They redirect customer flows through urban retail networks and redistribute welfare losses across neighborhoods. To measure this reorganization, we develop and validate a differentiable equilibrium model of store choice that estimates visit and welfare shifts after closures, using GPS mobility data linking 11,252 neighborhoods to 360 retail brands across five California metros. item.description: Research Square — Forests provide crucial ecosystem services, including climate regulation, biodiversity, and water conservation; however, forests are vulnerable to threats, including drought, climate change, wildfires, and resource extraction, such as mining. In response, forest managers utilize restoration strategies, including the installation of beaver dam analogs (BDAs) to improve water retention and reduce erosion. item.title: Addressing the biological and environmental dimensions of human reproductive decline
item.description: Frontiers in Science — Global fertility rates have declined rapidly and universally in recent decades and most nations now have rates below replacement level. This striking reversal from previous concerns about population explosion raises the question: is falling fertility driven primarily by social and cultural change or is biological fecundity—the intrinsic capacity to reproduce—also deteriorating? item.title: Anatomy of mapping urban greenery from a human perspective
item.description: Environmental Data Science — Urban greenery contributes to environmental sustainability, livability, and human well-being. As interest in human-centered urban environments has grown, researchers have increasingly sought to measure greenery as it is experienced by people rather than solely through conventional top-down representations. item.description: Journal of Political Economy — We provide new theory and evidence on the resilience of internal city structure after a large shock, analyzing the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Exploiting newly digitized data, we document that the city structure recovered within five years after the bombing. Our new dynamic quantitative model of internal city structure incorporates commuting, forward-looking location choices, migration frictions, agglomeration forces, and heterogeneous location fundamentals. item.description: E3S Web of Conferences — This paper provides a critical, integrated examination on the built environment of hot-arid Levantine cities, specifically evaluating its unintended, long-term impacts on human health. Gropius championed a functionalist architecture of standardization, extensive glazing, and flat roofs designed to maximize “sun, light, and air”. item.description: Routledge eBooks — Koodankulam, on India’s southern coast, has witnessed one of the country’s longest-running women-led antinuclear movements, which intensified in the wake of the 2011 Fukushima nuclear accident. Shared community spaces, conventionally sites of communal childcare and traditional livelihood practices, transformed into sites of exceptional protest when the communities were confronted with the imposition of a nuclear power plant. item.description: Population and Development Review — During the COVID‐19 pandemic, excess mortality rose sharply across Europe, with striking territorial disparities even within countries. This paper examines whether the characteristics of locally elected officials influenced excess mortality in Italy—one of the first countries severely affected. item.description: Frontiers in Psychology — Introduction This study focuses on older adults, a large and vulnerable population within China’s social structure, and draws upon risk perception theory and psychological resilience theory to examine the association between risk information exposure and psychological resilience among older adults. item.title: Green Infrastructure Development and Implications for Urban Sustainability, Public Health, and Climate Resilience, Al Khoud, Oman
item.description: E3S Web of Conferences — Rapid urban development in Oman, particularly in Al Khoud, Muscat, has placed increasing pressure on the environment, leading to a growing shortage of green space. This has raised concerns about urban heat, outdoor comfort, and the overall livability of urban areas. This study examines the current state of green infrastructure (GI) in Al Khoud and its contribution to a comfortable urban living environment. item.description: Jurnal Multidisiplin Indonesia — Slow-onset environmental degradation associated with open-pit tin mining and coastal ecosystem deterioration has transformed ecological conditions and livelihoods in extractive island regions. item.title: Geospatial Assessment of Rainfall-Triggered Landslide Risk Using Multi-Criteria Decision Techniques in Venezuela
item.description: Progress in landslide research and technology — Rainfall-induced landslides are a persistent threat in Venezuela due to a combination of varied topography, tropical rainfall and rapid urbanisation on alluvial fans and unstable hillslopes. This chapter aims to produce national Landslide Risk Index Maps (LRiM) to support disaster reduction initiatives in the country. item.description: Journal of Preventive Medicine and Holistic Health — The convergence of the Urban Heat Island (UHI) phenomenon, accelerating climate change, and unchecked urban expansion has produced a public health emergency of unprecedented scale across India. item.description: E3S Web of Conferences — Superblocks restrict through-traffic within groups of urban blocks and reallocate street space to walking, cycling, greenery, and public life. item.description: Frontiers in Energy Research — Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for urban decarbonization, yet their implementation requires integration across energy systems, buildings, mobility, and information and communication technologies, for which no coherent international standardization framework currently exists. item.description: Journal of Preventive Medicine and Holistic Health — As chronic disease, mental illness, metabolic disease, and aging populations rise in prevalence, there has been a shift from reactive healthcare to predictive and preventive medicine. item.title: Flexible but not free: The gendered flexibility paradox in Indonesia's gig economy
item.description: SIMULACRA JURNAL SOSIOLOGI — Female gig workers in Indonesia face challenges underexamined in a gig economy literature centered largely on Western contexts. Domestic scholarship has tended to treat gender as a descriptive variable within male-dominated sectors. This study examines how platform algorithms, gender norms, and household responsibilities shape women’s gig work across sectors. item.description: Frontiers in Sociology — Introduction Recurrent fires in South Africa's informal settlements are governed as technical emergencies, despite being produced and experienced through unequal infrastructures, insecure tenure, and uneven state protection. This study examines how young and older residents of fire-prone informal settlements in the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality interpret risk, respond to emergencies, negotiate recovery, and convert disaster experience into civic action. item.description: Environmental Research Communications — Extreme weather increasingly threatens the reliability of food supply chains, yet its relationship with transportation systems remains insufficiently quantified. We examine the associations between extreme weather exposure and U.S. food freight distribution using route-level truck shipment data from the Freight Analysis Framework (2018–2023) combined with high-resolution climate records. item.description: Population and Environment — Ambient air pollution is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including stillbirth, miscarriage, and preterm birth. However, its effects on the viability, implantation, and survival of conceptuses – largely unobserved before the clinical detection of pregnancy – remain poorly understood. item.description: PLOS Climate — Background Extreme heat and wildfire smoke events are increasing in frequency, severity, and geographic reach, placing compounding strain on healthcare systems and workers. item.description: MARGIN ECO — Hydrometeorological disasters cause not only physical damage but also substantial disruptions to livelihoods and local economic activities. This study examines the economic impacts of hydrometeorological disasters and identifies priority strategies for post-disaster economic recovery in West Sumatra, Indonesia. item.description: SIMULACRA JURNAL SOSIOLOGI — Makassar’s waste-to-energy (WtE) transition is promoted as a technological response to urban waste and clean-energy challenges, yet its social consequences remain insufficiently examined.
